ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
As shown in the figure is a schematic diagram of an experiment studying autonomous driving technology. On a straight highway, car A moves in a straight line towards the ultrasonic speed detector B. At time $t_{1}=0$, car A is at a distance $d_{1}=347.5\mathrm{m}$ from detector B. At this moment, detector B emits an ultrasonic signal and an infrared signal. Car A brakes upon receiving the infrared signal. When detector B receives the reflected ultrasonic signal, car A comes to a complete stop, at which point car A and detector B are separated by a distance $d_{2}=337.5\mathrm{m}$. The speed of the ultrasonic wave is known to be $v=340\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}$, and the speed of the infrared signal is much greater than that of the ultrasonic wave.

1. When car A receives the signal of the ultrasonic wave, its distance from the speed detector B is
2. The time it takes for Car A to come to a complete stop after braking.
3. The magnitude of the acceleration and initial velocity of car A during the braking process.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left side of the figure is the ultrasonic speed meter B, and on the right side is the car A. The car moves along a straight road toward B. The figure marks the distance d1 from B to the initial position of the car, and draws schematic arrows showing the propagation of infrared and ultrasonic signals between B and A; on the right side, a dashed line is also used to indicate the position of the car at another moment. The problem gives the initial distance d1=347.5 m, the distance when stopping d2=337.5 m, and the ultrasonic wave speed v=340 m/s. Reasoning: According to the specified method, let y(t) be the distance from car A to detector B, and let T be the time when the car stops, which is also the time when B receives the reflected ultrasonic wave. It is known that y(0)=d1=347.5 m, y(T)=d2=337.5 m, and the velocity when stopping is 0. The car decelerates uniformly to rest, so calculating the distance backward from the stopping moment: y(t)=d2+(1/2)a(T-t)^2, where a is the magnitude of the deceleration. Therefore d1-d2=(1/2)aT^2=10 m. The ultrasonic wave is emitted from B, reaches the car, is reflected, and then returns to B. According to the specified method, the time when the ultrasonic wave reaches the car is t=T/2, so the distance from the car to B at this time is x=y(T/2)=d2+(1/2)a(T/2)^2=d2+(d1-d2)/4=337.5+10/4=340 m. The total sound-path time satisfies T=2x/340=2×340/340=2 s. Then from d1-d2=(1/2)aT^2, we get 10=(1/2)a×2^2=2a, so a=5 m/s^2. The initial velocity v0=aT=5×2=10 m/s.
